svg.text: FinTracker: security and data handling, end to end
Follow the numbers: plan and classify first, then one user request from sign-in to AI answer, while every step is observed, retained or deleted by rule, and proven by tests.
How was the data classified, and what did it change?
How were secrets, credentials and access handled?
● built ○ designed / specified, not yet built
Plan and classify, before any code
Account/card numbers, bank credentials, tokens, files
Don't hold: last four only (D26); KMS; never logged
Transactions, balances, budgets, chats, AI summaries
Per-user RLS, encrypted, deleted on closure
IDs, counts and codes only; no amounts or prompts
Shared RAG index; the only text AI searches today
● Security: threat model per flow; ADRs (RLS, keys, internal API)
● Legal: GLBA, state laws in a control matrix (XS-COMP)
● Vendors: AWS attestations; Bedrock doesn't train on data
● AI risk: one service owns every LLM call (D4)
● after 5 failed tries, backoff to 15 min
● context; never body, path, LLM args
○ DB: IAM auth token, no password
○ CI: GitHub OIDC, no long-lived keys
● File never passes through a service
● Postgres RLS forced on every table
○ Last four only; card-like text masked
○ KMS customer key per data type;
○ only the owning role can decrypt
● Only service allowed to call an LLM
● Tools read-only; user fixed by token
● Untrusted text sent as JSON data
● RAG over public help docs only
● Per-user + app cost caps fail closed
answer or RFC 9457 error: a stable code + trace_id for support; never exception text or SQL
Observe and audit, at every step
● One trace_id per request, carried across every service (OpenTelemetry → X-Ray, CloudWatch)
● Audit events: audit(action, actor, resource, outcome) → /fintracker/audit (1 year dev, 2 years prod)
● CloudTrail records every AWS API call, including sign-in requests, with sub and source IP
● Logs carry IDs, counts and codes only: never amounts, prompts, model output or document text
○ Card-number mask on all log output; post-auth sign-in audit event; failed-sign-in alarm
○ Each service deletes only its share → UserDataDeleted;
○ alarm if not done in 7 days (inside the 45-day state window)
● Backups expire: Aurora 14 days, DynamoDB PITR 35 days,
● S3 old versions 7 days, disclosed in the privacy policy
Proving it works: every row ties a test to a requirement ID or an invariant
● RLS tests connect as a non-superuser
● a test named by requirement ID,
● number grounded in facts; live eval
● CI fails if a log line includes
